Google and Yelp review screen · Lafayette, Louisiana

Lafayette Racism Screen

Every review and owner reply on 1,401 Google Business Profiles was read and screened for allegations of racist treatment and for racist or racially coded language: all 132 profiles on Pinhook Rd and 1,269 across Northern Lafayette. Yelp reviews were then searched for every flagged business and the busiest others, 245 businesses in all. 138 profiles have at least one flagged review.

At a glance

  • 93 reviews on 62 profiles allege racist treatment outright: 11 profiles on Pinhook Rd and 51 in Northern Lafayette. 4 of those reviews are on Yelp, and 77 have no owner reply.
  • Pinhook Rd, most serious: Pizza Hut, 1821 W Pinhook Rd. Two 1 star reviews from August 2019, one written by a bystander, say a manager called a customer the N word. Neither has an owner reply.
  • Pinhook Rd, most flagged: Walmart Supercenter, 2428 W Pinhook Rd, with four direct allegations from 2017 to 2025, two loaded statements and three reviews calling the store or its staff ghetto.
  • Pinhook Rd, newest: Poupart Bakery, 1902 W Pinhook Rd. A review posted this month says a customer who came in later was served first and the reviewer was told they could leave; the reviewer believes that is how the bakery treats customers who are not white.
  • Northern Lafayette, most flagged: IHOP, 3230 NE Evangeline Thruway, with six direct allegations from 2018 to 2025: segregated seating, racist remarks from the kitchen, two Spanish language reviews saying Latino diners are treated badly, and two accounts from white diners. Two more are possible and four use coded language.
  • Northern Lafayette, one restaurant accused repeatedly: Julien’s Po Boys, 1900 W University Ave. Six Google reviews from 2018 and 2019 accuse the restaurant or its owner of racism, prejudice or bigotry, including a job applicant’s account, and the owner answered three of them by disputing or dismissing the review. On Yelp, a 2019 review says an older white man called the police on a customer who stopped in to use the phone and made sure officers knew the customer was Mexican, and a 2018 review cites offensive posters throughout the restaurant.
  • Northern Lafayette, one event: three reviews posted in May 2023, two apparently from the caterer, say the venue’s assistant at John Nickerson House Event Center rushed and harassed the guests and caterer at an April 2023 bridal shower and would not let the caterer cook in the kitchen; one says she did not want people of color there, and the caterer calls it discrimination. A fourth review from the same month says only: don’t be racist.
  • Northern Lafayette, newest direct allegations: McDonald’s, 1430 NE Evangeline Thruway (August 2026), where a customer says staff turned rude and racist toward the family, and the Starbucks counter inside Target, 3225 Louisiana Ave (April 2026).
  • Pinhook Rd on Yelp: 30 of the 46 businesses searched had a Yelp page that could be read. It adds one possible allegation, at Cajun Market Donut Company, 1812 W Pinhook Rd, where an Asian customer says the server who always waits on her treats her as an outsider and gives off a racist vibe; the shop is flagged only because of Yelp. It also adds one review calling the DoubleTree hotel a ghetto.
  • Northern Lafayette on Yelp: 120 of the 199 businesses searched had a Yelp page that could be read. It adds direct allegations at McDonald’s, 1430 NE Evangeline Thruway, where a traveling family says the all African American crew would not serve a white family; at CVS, 1315 Moss St Ext; and at Zydeco Ride & Shine Car Wash, 320 W Willow St, where a reviewer says the owner posted racist remarks about the community on Facebook. Zydeco Ride & Shine and Steven’s Fine Food & Seafood Market, the market for coded language only, are flagged only because of Yelp.
  • Owner replies: one reply repeats a slur. Popeyes, 200 E Willow St, thanked a reviewer by a display name containing a variant of the N word, in what reads as an automated reply.
  • What changed on Pinhook Rd: compared with the first version of this report, which did not read every review, Pinhook Rd now shows four more direct allegations (Poupart Bakery, Bargain Cars Lafayette and two at Walmart Supercenter), two more possible allegations and three more loaded statements.

Direct

Direct allegations of racist treatment

The reviewer says the treatment was racist or racially discriminatory, says race was the reason, describes white or fair skinned customers being helped as a pattern, or describes an unmistakably racial act. Allegations are summarized as written and have not been verified.

To reach a review, open the Maps profile, go to Reviews, and type a term shown into Search reviews. On hotel profiles, open All reviews and pick the Google filter first. The All reviews button opens the same list in Google Search. Reviews tagged Yelp are on the business’s Yelp page, where the Search reviews box finds them by the same terms.

2428 W Pinhook Rd · Department store · 4.0 on Google, 4,138 reviews

4 reviews
  • Google★★★★★1 starMay 2025No owner reply

    Describes two failed orders, one of them baby formula, and says the store manager was dismissive and rude, which the reviewer believes had to do with their skin color. Says a complaint went unanswered.

  • Google★★★★★1 starFeb 2025No owner reply

    Says security follows her every time she shops there and warns young Black women not to shop at this store.

  • Google★★★★★4 starsFeb 2025No owner reply

    A shopper says staff accused them of stealing, held them for more than three hours after closing without calling police, and kept over $1,000 in groceries. Calls the workers racist and says the harassment continues on later visits.

  • Google★★★★★4 starsNov 2017No owner reply

    A white shopper says employees and customers once told him the store was not for white people, that a pharmacy employee harassed white customers, and that Black cashiers let friends skip long lines. Says treatment has since improved.

Terms searched

Every Google review and owner reply was checked against 52 groups of terms, summarized in the six panels below; Yelp was searched with the twenty terms listed under Method. A match only brought a review up for reading; the tier it lands in was decided by reading it. Slurs are described by group rather than spelled out.

Allegation words

Words that name racism or bias outright, in every common form.

Judgment calls

Decisions that shape the counts above. Each can be reversed without redoing the screen.

  1. Allegations are reported as written. Nothing was verified with the businesses or the reviewers. Accounts that are secondhand, rest on one line with no detail, or carry a rating that does not fit the complaint are marked with a note.
  2. Yelp findings sit with Google’s. Each review carries a Google or Yelp tag and the counts above include both. A reviewer who told the same story on both sites is counted once per site.
  3. A Yelp page counts only when it matches. Where Yelp’s search offered another location or a similarly named business, the business is treated as having no Yelp page rather than borrowing that page’s reviews.
  4. Claims of bias against white customers count like any other. Several direct allegations claim bias against white customers, among them reviews at Walmart Supercenter on Pinhook Rd, IHOP, the Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles and CVS at 3754 Moss St, and on Yelp one at McDonald’s on NE Evangeline Thruway.
  5. A stated reason or a pattern counts as direct; a hint or a question counts as possible. A reviewer who says race was the reason, or describes white or fair skinned customers being helped as a pattern, is listed as direct. One who notes that a single white customer was greeted or thanked without saying race was the reason, asks whether race was the reason, or describes poor service and notes being the only Black diners without saying more, is listed as possible.
  6. One line allegations count. Reviews that say only racist, racists or full of racism are listed as direct allegations, each noted as giving no detail.
  7. Remarks by other customers are included and labeled. A racial remark by another diner (Cracker Barrel), customers using the N word (IHOP) and a look from another churchgoer (St. Genevieve) are listed because the reviewer reported them against the business.
  8. Language and accent. Mocking a named accent or language is treated as national origin bias; an accent the reviewer does not identify is listed as possible. Reviews built around staff not speaking English, or telling a business to speak English, are filed as loaded statements, as is an owner reply that blames a customer’s English. A neutral note that communication was hard is not counted.
  9. Other kinds of bias are not counted. Complaints about treatment based on gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability or insurance are listed under Not counted, as is a complaint about renter profiling at rental car chains.
  10. Ghetto, ratchet, hood and hood rat are treated as racially coded when aimed at staff, shoppers, a business or its neighborhood. Affectionate uses, a car hood, a dish apparently named the ghetto hot pocket, and thug used as a general insult were set aside. If you read these words as neutral slang, set that section aside.
  11. Racially charged imagery counts as loaded. A Confederate general’s portrait in a hotel room (Drury Inn & Suites) and a review describing a congregation’s support for the Confederate flag (Crossroads Church) are listed as loaded statements.
  12. An owner reply that repeats a slur is counted. Popeyes at 200 E Willow St thanked a reviewer by a display name containing a variant of the N word. The reply reads as automated but is published in the business’s voice. It is the only owner reply found with a slur.
  13. A mocking review is listed as loaded, not as an allegation. A five star review at Kevin’s Seafood written in a stereotyped accent claims bias against Asian customers and reads as mockery.
  14. A review posted on the wrong profile is set aside. A KD Seafood Express review that names Kevin’s Seafood, which the owner says belongs to another business, is not counted against KD.
  15. Repeated reviews count separately. Near duplicates at Burger King on Pinhook Rd and Blue Star Inn, and three reviews about one event at John Nickerson House, two apparently from the same caterer, are each counted and noted.
  16. Northern Lafayette boundary. Profiles with a Lafayette address north of latitude 30.2305, roughly the Cameron St line, were included up to the Carencro and Scott limits. Downtown addresses south of that line and profiles with a Carencro or Scott address were not; a few included profiles carry Downtown or Carencro in their names.
  17. Pinhook Rd includes two Broussard addresses. Evangeline Veterinary Clinic (3730 W Pinhook Rd) and Dollar General (3741 W Pinhook Rd) are on Pinhook but carry Broussard addresses. Neither was flagged.

Method and limits

How the screen worked

  • Pinhook Rd roster: all 132 Google Business Profiles with an E or W Pinhook Rd address, gathered from 50 Google Maps category searches along the road. 125 have reviews.
  • Northern Lafayette roster: 176 Google Maps category searches across the city returned 6,933 profiles. The 1,269 with a Lafayette address north of latitude 30.2305, roughly the Cameron St line, are included. 1,066 have reviews.
  • Reading: every review Google returned for each profile was read, at every star rating, with its owner reply: 33,856 on Pinhook Rd and 129,886 in Northern Lafayette, against 163,750 in Google’s headline counts.
  • Screening: each review and owner reply was checked against the 52 term groups summarized above. 604 matched at least one term, and every match was read in full and placed by hand.
  • Second read: misspellings, Spanish terms and plural race nouns such as blacks or whites were added partway through, so every profile was read a second time with the final list.
  • Yelp: every business flagged on Google (135) and the 110 others with the most Google reviews, 170 or more, were looked up on Yelp by name and address. 150 Yelp pages were matched and read, all on name and street number except one tire shop whose Yelp page lists no address, 29 were found but their review search did not load, and 66 businesses had no matching page. Each page was searched with Yelp’s own review search for twenty terms: racist, racism, racial, racially, raciest, discrimination, discriminated, discriminate, prejudice, prejudiced, bigot, bigotry, profiled, profiling, stereotyped, segregated, slur, ghetto, ratchet and racista. Yelp also returns near forms such as profile, so all 19 matches were read in full and placed with the same rules as the Google reviews.

What it cannot see

  • Reviews Google has removed or filtered are not visible.
  • Hotel profiles on Google also show reviews from booking sites; only reviews written on Google were read there.
  • Yelp covers only the flagged businesses and the busiest others. The plan was every flagged business plus every other business with 50 or more Google reviews, 428 in all, but after 245 Yelp asked for a human verification check and the search stopped there rather than try to get past it. On 29 Yelp pages the review search did not load, so they were not read. Only twenty terms were searched on Yelp, and reviews Yelp marks as not recommended were not searched.
  • Nextdoor is not covered. Its neighborhood posts are shown only to verified residents signed in to a personal account.
  • Spanish terms were searched directly. Reviews in other languages were screened through the English translation Google supplies, when it supplies one.
  • Not screened: photos, owner posts, questions and answers, business descriptions and profile attributes.
  • Dates come from Google’s timestamps. For an edited review the date may be the edit date.
  • The rosters come from category searches and may miss small offices in shared buildings or businesses without a matching category.
  • Reviewer and employee names are left out.
Lafayette Racism Screen · Google Business Profiles on Pinhook Rd and across Northern Lafayette, Louisiana, with Yelp for flagged and busy businesses · Reviews read Sep 26, 2026
